subject: rea
title: wrong zero preload counts on a 100 MB Electron app
fix: JS graph built file by file with per-file budgets in tables (§3.8); a budget hit marks coverage partial with a named limit, never a zero count (§3.5); a large Electron fixture gets a count test.
note: Source is search snippets only; the report is unconfirmed.

subject: rea
title: slower than a plain agent on a simple Mac app
fix: Built-in readers on a reserved cheap lane (§3.7) answer simple-app questions without an engine; the Phase 1 gate requires beating leanrea Tier 0 on the cheap-question subset (§9).
note: Source is search snippets only; unconfirmed.

subject: rea
title: frontier models refusing RE prompts
fix: Not in the plan: record model refusals per arm in the benchmark (§10) and state the lawful-analysis scope from scope.md (§13) in the generated skill and tool descriptions (§4).
note: Model behaviour, not a tool bug; kind is a best fit.

subject: rea
title: output is pseudocode, not original source (README.md:304-306 agrees)
fix: Wont candidate, not yet reviewed: Recovering original source from compiled code is not possible in general; reax labels pseudocode rather than promising source. Decompiler output is labelled engine-derived pseudocode with engine and version (§3.5 cache key); source-to-artifact comparison (§8 C44) is the route when original source exists.

subject: rea
title: Compared with Binary Ninja MCP (GPL-3.0): Binary Ninja IL levels (HLIL/MLIL/LLIL, SSA); retyping, prototypes, byte patching; switching between several open binaries

fix: Wont candidate, not yet reviewed: Binary Ninja is commercial with no open equal (§8 reviewed wont), and byte patching is excluded by §13. Binary Ninja provider is a reviewed wont (§8); retyping and prototypes come through annotate on Ghidra (§3.5); byte patching is out of scope (§0, §13); multiple open targets are daemon sessions (§3.3).

subject: rea
title: Compared with binwalk v3 (MIT, Rust): Own signature scanner over many formats; entropy analysis; usable as a Rust library

subject: rea
title: Compared with electronegativity (Apache-2.0, archived; successor ElectroNG): Grades Electron apps against the Electron security checklist (contextIsolation, dangerous functions, CSP…); outputs CSV/SARIF; accepts directories and ASAR

subject: rea
title: Compared with GhidraMCP (Apache-2.0): Renames methods and data in a live Ghidra project; headless mode saves changes between runs
evidence: rea's Ghidra projects are temporary and deleted on close (SECURITY.md:38-43). No persistent annotation
fix: annotate writes to persistent Ghidra projects under REAX_HOME/projects/<digest>/<engine>/ with set semantics and read-back (§3.5); Phase 2 gate checks annotations survive a daemon restart (§9).

subject: rea
title: Compared with ida-pro-mcp (MIT): Patching (patch, patch_asm), set_type/declare_type, idb_save, py_eval; headless supervisor with up to 4 database workers; debugger extension
evidence: rea uses ida-pro-mcp as its IDA backend but keeps IDA read-only (AGENTS.md:9)
fix: IDA is a commercial adapter behind an ownership gate and protocol fakes (§9 Phase 2); set_type and save map to annotate (§3.5); patching is out of scope; py_eval and the debugger are not planned.
note: Row mixes in-scope items (types, save) with excluded ones (patch, patch_asm per §0/§13); split it if the lead wants a wont for the patching half.

subject: rea
title: Compared with jadx (Apache-2.0): GUI with search and usages, smali debugger, deobfuscation with mapping files, Gradle project export, plugin marketplace

fix: Not in the plan: add JADX mapping-file input and Gradle project export to the JADX adapter (§8 C24); the GUI, smali debugger and plugin marketplace do not apply to an agent tool.

subject: rea
title: Compared with radare2-mcp (MIT): Read-only mode (-R); per-tool enable/disable; sandbox settings; supervisor approvals; HTTP bearer auth; per-session multiplexing

fix: Read tools split from mutating tools (§3.4), approval queue (§0), HTTP bearer token (§3.3), daemon serving many clients (§3.3). Not in the plan: a per-operation allow-list in configuration.

subject: rea
title: Compared with ReVa (Apache-2.0): Renames variables and fixes data types inside Ghidra; works across many programs in one project; optional PyGhidra scripting; small tool results with links to limit "context rot"
evidence: No Ghidra write-back; one deep binding per target per connection; large default results (A4)
fix: Ghidra write-back via annotate on persistent projects (§3.5); several targets per daemon session (§3.3); small results with handles and resource_link (§0).

subject: rea

fix: Rules run on @ast-grep/napi (§6), but the plan names only reax-authored rules. Not in the plan: accept user-supplied ast-grep rule files in analyze (§5).
